name: What is the best way to choose tile for a primary bathroom shower?

mainEntity.name: How do I pick shower tile that looks high-end but is still practical for a primary bathroom?
mainEntity.text: How do I pick shower tile that looks high-end but is still practical for a primary bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing shower tile for a primary bathroom is about more than style. The best tile should be durable, appropriate for wet areas, and easy to maintain. Porcelain is often the most practical choice because it resists moisture and comes in many finishes, including stone-look and slab-look options. Large-format tile can create a cleaner, more upscale appearance and reduce grout lines. The shower floor needs special care because drainage and slope requirements matter more there than on walls. Not every tile size works equally well in the pan. Homeowners should also think about cleaning, grout color, and whether the tile choice fits the overall design of the bathroom. A visually strong shower often comes from combining simple, high-quality materials with precise installation rather than using overly busy patterns.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best shower tile balances slip resistance, water performance, maintenance, and style. Porcelain is usually the safest choice for durability, while large-format tile can reduce grout lines and simplify cleaning. The shower floor needs special attention because very large tile may not work well there without proper slope and drainage design.
